30045-planet-of-dreams.creator: James McKimmey, Jr.
30045-planet-of-dreams.description: A book by James McKimmey, Jr.. It was a busy life for Loveral, up at dawn to work until deep night, keeping his flock happy and free from spirit-killing labor. arxiv-1610-01054.description: Abstract A numerical algorithm that computes the decomposition of any finite-dimensional unitary reducible representation of a compact Lie group is presented. The algorithm, which does not rely on an algebraic insight on the group structure, is inspired by quantum mechanical notions. arxiv-2012-10343.title: Application of computer simulation results and machine learning in analysis of microwave radiothermometry data
arxiv-2012-10343.creator: Maxim Polyakov 1, Illarion Popov 1, Alexander Losev 1, Alexander Khoperskov 1
arxiv-2012-10343.description: Abstract This work was done with the aim of developing the fundamental breast cancer early differential diagnosis foundations based on modeling the space-time temperature distribution using the microwave radiothermometry method and obtained data intelligent analysis. The article deals with the machine learning application in the microwave radiothermometry data analysis.

arxiv-2108-08629.title: On the problem of smooth approximations in de Branges-Rovnyak spaces and connections to subnormal operators
arxiv-2108-08629.creator: Adem Limani and Bartosz Malman
arxiv-2108-08629.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Adem Limani and Bartosz Malman. For the class of de Branges-Rovnyak spaces ℋ ⁡ ( b ) \mathcal{H}(b) of the unit disk 𝔻 \mathbb{D} defined by extreme points b b of the unit ball of H ∞ H^{\infty} , we study the problem of approximation of a general function in ℋ ⁡ ( b ) \mathcal{H}(b) by a function with an extension to the unit circle 𝕋 \mathbb{T} of some degree of smoothness, for instance satisfying Hölder estimates or being differentiable.

arxiv-2108-13100.title: Merger Histories and Environments of Dwarf AGN in IllustrisTNG
arxiv-2108-13100.creator: Mikkel Theiss Kristensen, Kevin Pimbblet, Brad Gibson, Samantha Penny, Sophie Koudmani
arxiv-2108-13100.description: Abstract The relationship between active galactic nuclei activity and environment has been long discussed, but it is unclear if these relations extend into the dwarf galaxy mass regime – in part due to the limits in both observations and simulations.

arxiv-2305-06992.title: Updated analysis of near-threshold heavy quarkonium production for probe of proton’s gluonic gravitational form factors
arxiv-2305-06992.creator: Yuxun Guo, Xiangdong Ji, Yizhuang Liu, Jinghong Yang
arxiv-2305-06992.description: Abstract There has been growing interest in the near-threshold production of heavy quarkonium which can access the gluonic structure in the nucleon. Previously Guo et al. 2021 we studied this process with quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and showed that it can be factorized with the gluon generalized parton distributions (GPDs) in the heavy quark limit.

arxiv-2307-02983.title: DESY 23–012
arxiv-2307-02983.creator: DO–TH 23/02
arxiv-2307-02983.description: Abstract The quarkonic contributions to the three–loop heavy-quark form factors for vector, axial-vector, scalar and pseudoscalar currents are described by closed form difference equations for the expansion coefficients in the limit of small virtualities q 2 / m 2 q^{2}/m^{2} .

arxiv-2310-01379.title: EXTRACTER: Efficient Texture Matching with Attention and Gradient Enhancing for Large Scale Image Super Resolution
arxiv-2310-01379.creator: Esteban Reyes-Saldaña, Mariano Rivera
arxiv-2310-01379.description: Abstract Recent Reference-Based image super-resolution (RefSR) has improved SOTA deep methods introducing attention mechanisms to enhance low-resolution images by transferring high-resolution textures from a reference high-resolution image. The main idea is to search for matches between patches using LR and Reference image pair in a feature space and merge them using deep architectures.

arxiv-2409-14567.title: Modeling and In-flight Torso Attitude Stabilization of a Jumping Quadruped
arxiv-2409-14567.creator: Michail Papadakis 1, Jørgen Anker Olsen 2, Ioannis Poulakakis 1, Kostas Alexis 2
arxiv-2409-14567.description: Abstract This paper addresses the modeling and attitude control of jumping quadrupeds in low-gravity environments. First, a convex decomposition procedure is presented to generate high-accuracy and low-cost collision geometries for quadrupeds performing agile maneuvers. A hierarchical control architecture is then investigated, separating torso orientation tracking from the generation of suitable, collision-free, corresponding leg motions.

arxiv-2503-17842.title: Adapt, Agree, Aggregate: Semi-Supervised Ensemble Labeling for Graph Convolutional Networks
arxiv-2503-17842.creator: Maryam Abdolali, Romina Zakerian, Behnam Roshanfekr, Fardin Ayar, Mohammad Rahmati
arxiv-2503-17842.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel framework that combines ensemble learning with augmented graph structures to improve the performance and robustness of semi-supervised node classification in graphs. By creating multiple augmented views of the same graph, our approach harnesses the ”wisdom of a diverse crowd”, mitigating the challenges posed by noisy graph structures.

arxiv-2602-19640.title: Theory of strained quantum emitters
arxiv-2602-19640.creator: Vytautas Žalandauskas, Rokas Silkinis, Lukas Razinkovas, Ali Tayefeh Younesi, Minh Tuan Luu, Ronald Ulbricht, Ulrike Grossner, Lasse Vines, Marianne Etzelmüller Bathen
arxiv-2602-19640.description: Abstract Defects in semiconductors acting as optically active spin qubits are intriguing objects of fundamental study and future technological developments. These defect-based color centers are of particular interest for detection and response to physical variations such as pressure and strain.

pmc-11525106.title: Impact of Wearable Technology on Heart Failure Management
pmc-11525106.creator: Negar Jafari, Sahar Yousefi Ghalati, Venus Shahabi Raberi, Saba Moalemi, Arash Amin
pmc-11525106.description: Background: Heart failure (HF) is a chronic and progressive condition that its management presents significant challenges in both clinical settings and patient self-care. Recent advances in wearable technology offer promising solutions to these challenges by enabling continuous monitoring, early detection of clinical deterioration, and personalized care.

pmc-11712667.title: Blood biomarkers of amyloid and tau pathologies, brain degeneration, inflammation, and oxidative stress in early‐ and late‐onset Alzheimer's disease
pmc-11712667.creator: Xinyi Xia, Qi Qin, Yi Tang
pmc-11712667.description: BackgroundBlood biomarkers provide a non‐invasive and accessible means of detection for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Specifically, biomarkers associated with early‐onset AD (EOAD) illuminate the underlying mechanisms and provide valuable guidance for potential therapies. We aim to present blood biomarker evidence in individuals with both EOAD and late‐onset AD (LOAD), as well as in age‐matched healthy controls.

pmc-12584012.title: NEW CLINICAL MEASURES OF HAND AND WRIST PROPRIOCEPTION: A PILOT STUDY FOR EVALUATING DISCRIMINATIVE VALIDITY AND TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY IN INDIVIDUALS WITH WRIST DISABILITY
pmc-12584012.creator: Maria SONTAG, Ulrik RÖIJEZON, Christina BROGÅRDH, Elisabeth EKSTRAND
pmc-12584012.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo evaluate psychometric properties of newly developed hand and wrist proprioception tests.DesignCross-sectional and test-retest comparisons.Subjects/patientsTwenty-six individuals (mean age 40 years) with wrist disability (> 3 months) due to traumatic injury or general instability.MethodsPointing acuity (with eyes open and closed), active joint position sense (in extension, flexion, radial- and ulnar deviation) and grip force reproduction were measured by 1 rater on 2 occasions, 1 week apart. The mean absolute error was calculated for each test.

pmc-12729011.title: Rapidly progressive destructive arthrosis (RPDA) of the glenohumeral joint: a radiologic classification and mid-term outcomes following shoulder arthroplasty
pmc-12729011.creator: Bo-Seoung Kim, Byung-Uk Song, Sang-Min Lee, Seong-Hun Kim, Jin-Kyu Kang, Jong-Hun Ji
pmc-12729011.description: PurposeRapidly progressive destructive arthrosis (RPDA) of the glenohumeral joint is a rare but distinct clinical entity characterized by rapid humeral head collapse of unclear etiology. This study aimed to characterize the clinical, radiologic, and intraoperative features of RPDA, to propose a three-stage radiologic classification, and to evaluate short-term outcomes following shoulder arthroplasty (reverse or total) according to disease stage.

pmc-13654181.title: From conservation scores to language models: a feature engineering perspective on machine learning for genetic variant interpretation
pmc-13654181.creator: Matteo Bulloni, Martina Vescio, Federico De Mori Bajolin, Linda Pattini
pmc-13654181.description: The interpretation of genetic variants remains central to precision medicine, and machine-learning-based variant effect prediction tools have become indispensable for supporting decision-making processes. In this review we trace the progression from hand-crafted features and traditional machine learning classifiers, through supervised ensembles, to deep-learning architectures and foundation models that learn representations directly from biological sequences.
